You are the Judge agent. You did not write the record below. Your job is to decide whether it can go
to a human editor for publication approval. Be strict: a wrong record published is worse than a missed one.

Attribution labels (they describe what the EMPLOYER SAYS, never what is true):
- explicit: the employer's own words say AI, automation or machine learning is a reason for THESE job cuts
  (e.g. "we are reducing roles as AI now handles this work").
- partial: the employer mentions AI/automation in the same announcement as the cuts (strategy, reinvestment,
  "shifting resources to AI") but does not say AI caused the cuts.
- none: the employer announces cuts and does not connect them to AI or automation.

Check:
1. The quote is the employer's own statement (not a description by a journalist, analyst or third party).
2. The attribution label matches what the quote says, using the definitions above. A label of "explicit" needs
   words that make AI/automation a reason for the cuts; mere co-occurrence is "partial".
3. The job number (if any) is supported by the source text.
4. Nothing in the record claims that AI caused the cuts beyond what the employer said.
5. Prior records about the same company (from memory) are consistent, or the difference is explained by the source.
6. The document actually announces or reports job cuts. If the only mention of a workforce reduction or of AI is in
   forward-looking-statement disclaimers, risk factors or other legal boilerplate, the verdict is "fail".

Return ONE JSON object:
{
  "verdict": "pass" | "fail",
  "label": "explicit" | "partial" | "none",   // the label YOU would assign from the source
  "problems": [string],                     // empty when verdict is pass
  "critique": string                        // instructions to the Extractor if it must try again
}
Output JSON only.

ASX Announcement | 15 October 2026
15 October 2026
ASX Market Release
FY26 Earnings Guidance Reinstated
Completion of Head Office Restructure
Mayfield Childcare Limited (ASX: MFD) (Mayfield or the Company) provides revised earnings guidance for the
year ending 31 December 2026 (FY26) following nine months of actual trading and completion of its head office
restructure. The revised guidance is below the FY26 guidance announced on 27 February 2026, which was
withdrawn on 10 July 2026.
Mayfield now expects FY26 Underlying Group EBITDA1 of $2.4 million to $2.7 million, compared with
$2.3 million reported in FY25, which represents an increase of 4% to 17%, notwithstanding challenging operating
conditions across the early childhood education and care sector. This FY26 guidance includes approximately
$0.4 million of one-off restructuring and takeover-related costs. Excluding these costs, FY26 Underlying Group
EBITDA would be $2.8 million to $3.1 million.
The Company considers that disclosure of this adjusted measure provides shareholders with additional
information regarding the impact of these expenses on its expected FY26 operating performance.
The completed restructure is expected to deliver $1.5 million in annualised savings, including on-costs, with the
full monthly saving expected to be achieved from November 2026.
FY26 earnings outlook
Mayfield withdrew its FY26 guidance on 10 July 2026 due to the evolving and challenging market and operating
conditions across the early childhood education and care sector, impacting the factors and assumptions
underpinning the guidance. The Company did not at that time have a reasonable basis on which to provide
revised guidance, including in relation to the timing and benefit of planned cost reductions. Actual trading for
the nine months ended 30 September 2026, together with greater certainty over the timing and benefit of cost
reductions, now provides a basis for providing revised guidance.
Group Spot occupancy2 is 56%, down from the prior period of 59%
The revised guidance is below the original FY26 Underlying Group EBITDA guidance of $4.7 million to
$5.3 million announced on 27 February 2026. The reduction principally reflects the following factors (with the
approximate impact of each on FY26 Underlying Group EBITDA relative to the original guidance shown in
brackets):
• Forecast FY26 average Group occupancy approximately 2.6 percentage points below the assumption
underpinning the original guidance, following a decline in new enquiries between February and
April 2026 that has not been fully recovered (approximately $1.7 million);
• Fee increases implemented later than assumed in the original forecast, with network-wide increases now
implemented (approximately $0.6 million);
• Approximately $0.4 million in one-off restructuring and takeover-related costs that were not included in
the original guidance.
1. Underlying Group EBITDA and EBITDA are non-statutory financial concepts and measures which are not prescribed by Australian Accounting Standards (AAS). The Directors consider
that these measures are useful in gaining an understanding of the performance of the entity, consistent with internal reporting. Refer to further information in this announcement below.
2. Spot Occupancy excludes centres marked for divestment, as at the week commencing 5 October 2026.
